title: Skid Steer Loader Safety
summary: Skid steer loaders put operators and nearby workers at risk of falls, crushing, pinning, and struck-by injuries. This talk covers safety devices, staying in the cab, and keeping others clear.
talking_points: Use and maintain the manufacturer's safety devices: interlocked controls, backup alarms, seat belts, Roll Over Protective Structure (ROPS), and lift arm supports.
Run the loader only from the operator's compartment, never from outside. Stay seated with the seat belt fastened and the restraint bar in place.
Keep your arms, legs, and head inside the cab while operating.
Never leave the machine with the engine running or the lift arms raised unless the lift arm supports are in place.
Load, unload, and turn on level, stable ground when possible.
Keep other workers out of the work area while you lift a load.
site_hazards_to_check: Bypassed or broken interlocks, backup alarm, or ROPS
Operator reaching in from outside the cab to work the controls
Lift arms raised with no lift arm supports installed
Sloped, soft, or uneven ground where the loader is lifting or turning
Workers standing in front of or beside the loader during a lift
discussion_questions: Which safety devices on this loader must work before it goes into service?
Why is operating the controls from outside the cab so dangerous?
How do we keep ground workers clear of the loader today?

No tolerance issues.
